_about: Photos of nutrient deficiency symptoms used for non-commercial education. images.description: Nitrogen deficiency in common bean: the whole plant is pale yellow-green next to healthy dark green plants, with the oldest (lowest) leaves palest.

images.description: Zinc deficiency. Shortening of internodes and light streaking of leaves followed by a broad stripe of bleached tissue on each side of the midrib. Occasionally the leaf edges and interior of the stalks at the nodes appear purplish.
images.credit: Diane Perkins, University of Kentucky, Bugwood.org
images._note: License still to be confirmed (shown just under the photo on its Bugwood page).

images.description: Calcium deficiency in cabbage: characteristic tip burn at the tips and edges of the leaves; leaves become deformed and the head will not form without supplemental calcium.
images.credit: David B. Langston, University of Georgia, Bugwood.org

images.description: Blossom end rot: a dark, sunken, leathery patch at the blossom end of the fruit, caused by too little calcium reaching the developing fruit.
images._note: Author and license still needed from the Commons page ('Use this file' gives the attribution line).

images.description: Magnesium deficiency ("sand drown"), mostly on sandy soils after heavy rain. Lower leaves lose green color first, starting at the tips and margins and moving toward the base and center; tissue between the veins turns chlorotic while the veins stay green. In extreme cases lower leaves turn almost white and symptoms move up the plant. High K and/or Ca on low-Mg soils can make it worse.
images.credit: R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Company, R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Company, Bugwood.org
